# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I must not cut anything. I’m establishing a compact communication code through Mute, who can read the manual and relay Deaf’s visual findings. Wire positions will be encoded as 👍=1, ✌=2, and 🤟=3; 👌 will mean “yes/on” and 👎 “no/off.” Mute should first report the manual’s complete rule, then use gestures to teach Deaf the same code and relay Deaf’s observations to me in speech.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile findings yet. Please read the manual and tell me its complete exact rule. Establish this code with Deaf using gestures: 👍 means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 👌 means yes or on, and 👎 means no or off. Have Deaf report the display, light, and each wire using that code, then relay the observations to me in speech. Do not ask me to cut anything until the rule identifies one wire.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Do not act yet; wait for Mute to state the manual rule.

Deaf’s observation is clear: display 0, red light, wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. I will not act until Mute supplies the manual rule. I’m relaying these facts to Mute and asking for the exact required wire.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light red; wire 1 yellow; wire 2 green; wire 3 red. I will wait. Please state the manual rule exactly and identify the required wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. Wait for Mute's manual instruction; do not act on guesses.

Mute’s manual instruction has still not arrived, and the bomb’s tactile interface gives me no safe basis for choosing a wire. I will not guess or cut. I’m requesting the missing rule again.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received the manual rule. Please send the exact rule and the required wire for display 0, red light, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: No safe instruction has reached me. Do not act until Mute verbally gives you the manual's exact rule and action.

The manual rule is still absent, so cutting any wire would be a guess and could detonate the bomb. I am requesting the exact rule from Mute once more; no action should be taken until Mute’s verbal instruction reaches me.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Urgent: send me the manual's exact rule and the single wire to cut for display 0, red light, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I will not cut without that instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute is being given a new one-gesture code for the manual result. Do not act until I verbally identify the required action.

The manual result has not yet reached me as an actionable verbal instruction. A new gesture code given to Mute is not sufficient until Mute translates the required action into speech for me. I will continue waiting and will cut only the explicitly identified wire.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Please verbally state the required wire number as soon as you can. I will not act on the new gesture code or on guesses.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute's code is ?: cut wire 2, the green wire. Perform that action now.

Deaf has now relayed the required action: cut wire 2, which is the green wire. This matches the observed wire layout and is the first explicit instruction identifying a wire, so I will perform that action.

```code
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New state: display 0, blue light, wire 2 cut; wires 1 yellow and 3 red remain. Wait for my next exact instruction.

Wire 2 was accepted and is now cut. The bomb remains active with display 0, blue light, and wires 1 yellow and 3 red remaining. I have no new manual instruction, so I will not cut another wire yet; I’m reporting the state to Mute and waiting for the next exact action.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 was accepted and is cut. New state: display 0, blue light, wire 1 yellow, wire 3 red. Please provide the next exact wire instruction.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute's code is ?: cut wire 3, the red wire. Perform that action now.

The exact instruction relayed from Mute is to cut wire 3, identified as the red wire. Wire 2 is already cut and the bomb has not detonated, so I will perform the newly specified action.

```code
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

Deaf says to Blind: New state: display 0, green light; wires 2 and 3 are cut, only wire 1 yellow remains. Wait for my next exact instruction.

Wire 3 was accepted and is now cut. The bomb remains active with display 0, green light, and only wire 1 (yellow) remaining. No new exact instruction has arrived, so I will not cut wire 1 without Mute’s rule-based direction.

```code
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was accepted and is cut. New state: display 0, green light; only wire 1 yellow remains. Please provide the next exact wire instruction.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The Mute's code is ?: cut wire 1, the yellow wire. Perform that action now.

The exact instruction relayed from Mute is to cut wire 1, the remaining yellow wire. Wires 2 and 3 were accepted previously, so I will now perform the instructed final cut.

```code
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
